description.value: A longitudinal resting-state fMRI study describing large-scale functional-network abnormalities in unmedicated patients with schizophrenia and examining changes after six weeks of risperidone treatment.

spans.text: 34 unmedicated patients with schizophrenia and 34 matched healthy controls were enrolled in this longitudinal study. We collected resting state functional MRI data with a 3T scanner at baseline and six weeks after they were started on risperidone. In addition, a group of 19 healthy controls were scanned twice six weeks apart.

value: large scale functional networks to be differentially affected in unmedicated patients
network integrity would be, at least partially, restored after six weeks of antipsychotic treatment

spans.text: Based on the existing literature, we hypothesized large scale functional networks to be differentially affected in unmedicated patients and that network integrity would be, at least partially, restored after six weeks of antipsychotic treatment.

clinical_characteristics.value: 34 subjects; 22 chronically ill and 12 first episode; 17 antipsychotic-naive and 17 previously exposed; all were off antipsychotic medication for at least ten days at baseline.

spans.text: Of the 34 SZ subjects, 22 were chronically ill and 12 experienced their first episode. 17 SZ were antipsychotic naïve (five had not received prior treatment despite a prolonged period since illness onset), and 17 have had prior exposure to antipsychotic medication.
Twelve subjects were concomitantly treated with benztropine, two with trazodone, one each was prescribed mirtazapine, amitriptyline, and valproic acid.
